descriptionChirho: The abstract noun denoting hope, expectation, or anticipated outcome. All four clusters represent the same lexical sense with mere grammatical variation (construct state, pronominal suffixes 1cs/3ms, conjunctive waw). Spanish uniformly renders 'esperanza,' Arabic uses 'رَجَاء' and 'تَوَقُّع' (both meaning hope/expectation), Hindi uses 'आशा' and 'प्रत्याशा' (hope/anticipation), Korean uses '소망' (hope) and '기대' (expectation), and Swahili consistently uses 'tumaini' (hope). The slight variation between 'hope' and 'expectation' in English/Arabic reflects register, not a distinct sense.
